bugs.name: A private repository keeps 'Anonymous Read' and shows both 'Private' and 'Public Access' badges
bugs.summary: The repository is Private but the Code unit still has \"Anonymous Read\" selected, and the page states \"Anonymous Read: users who are not logged in can access the unit with read permission\" — i.e. the code of a private repository is declared readable by visitors who are not logged in. The repository header simultaneously shows a \"Private\" badge and an orange \"Public Access\" badge. Saving the same override directly on the private repository is accepted with \"The repository settings have been updated.\" and no warning. (on /eval/agent5-vis-probe/settings/public_access)
bugs.expected: A private repository is reachable by allowed members only: the Danger Zone says making it private will \"make the repo visible to only allowed members\", so the public-visitor permissions should be refused, cleared, or warned about, and the repository should read as Private only — not also advertise \"Public Access\".
bugs.actual: The repository is Private but the Code unit still has \"Anonymous Read\" selected, and the page states \"Anonymous Read: users who are not logged in can access the unit with read permission\" — i.e. the code of a private repository is declared readable by visitors who are not logged in. The repository header simultaneously shows a \"Private\" badge and an orange \"Public Access\" badge. Saving the same override directly on the private repository is accepted with \"The repository settings have been updated.\" and no warning.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, open https://5503-imv8yr62nz49o7qx2vsk0.e2b.app/eval/agent5-vis-probe/settings/public_access (public repo I created, agent5-vis-probe).
In the row for unit "Code" select the "Anonymous Read" radio button and click "Update Settings" (message: "The repository settings have been updated.").
Open /eval/agent5-vis-probe/settings, scroll to the "Danger Zone", click "Make Private" and confirm with "Yes" (message: "Repository visibility changed.").
bugs.reason: Deliberate 1.24 feature: public-access overrides are meant to apply on top of the repository visibility ('Configure public visitor's access permissions to override the defaults of this repository'). The header template prints the orange 'Public Access' label independently of the Private label, and the permission code applies the anonymous unit modes even after the 'anonymous user visit private repo' branch.

bugs.name: Escape does not close the 'Delete Branch Protection' confirm dialog
bugs.summary: The \"Delete Branch Protection\" dialog stays open after Escape (pressed twice); the only way out is clicking \"No\". Focus moves to \"No\" and then \"Yes\" with Tab, and no console error is logged. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/settings/branches)
bugs.expected: Escape closes the confirm dialog and nothing is deleted, the way Escape closes the other confirmation dialogs in the same settings area (e.g. \"Delete This Repository\" and \"Archive This Repo\" on /eval/harbor-handbook/settings, and the \"Visibility\" dialog).
bugs.actual: The \"Delete Branch Protection\" dialog stays open after Escape (pressed twice); the only way out is clicking \"No\". Focus moves to \"No\" and then \"Yes\" with Tab, and no console error is logged.
reproSteps: Open https://5503-imv8yr62nz49o7qx2vsk0.e2b.app/eval/harbor-handbook/settings/branches while signed in as eval.
If no branch protection rule is listed, click "Add New Rule", type pattern agent15-eval-* in "Protected Branch Name Pattern" and click "Save Rule".
Click "Delete Rule" next to the rule to open the "Delete Branch Protection" dialog.
Press the Escape key once, then a second time.
bugs.reason: Deliberate: the generic delete-button confirm dialog is opened with closable: false, which in Fomantic disables both outside-click and Escape dismissal, so the user must answer No or Yes. The Danger Zone dialogs use a different helper (show-modal) without that option, which explains the difference.

bugs.name: After sign-out the browser Back button re-displays the cached repository Settings page
bugs.summary: Back after sign-out re-displays the whole repository Settings page of the signed-out account, including the Repository Name, Description and Danger Zone controls, with the signed-in navigation bar. The page is served from the browser's back cache (the navigation answers 200 without asking the server), so only a manual Reload replaces it with the Sign In page. Seen twice out of two tries (once on the settings page of eval/harbor-handbook, once more after signing out and going Back again). (on /eval/harbor-handbook/settings)
bugs.expected: After signing out, going Back must not show the account's repository settings page again — the sign-out should invalidate the page so Back lands on the sign-in page (as a reload of the same address does).
bugs.actual: Back after sign-out re-displays the whole repository Settings page of the signed-out account, including the Repository Name, Description and Danger Zone controls, with the signed-in navigation bar. The page is served from the browser's back cache (the navigation answers 200 without asking the server), so only a manual Reload replaces it with the Sign In page. Seen twice out of two tries (once on the settings page of eval/harbor-handbook, once more after signing out and going Back again).
reproSteps: Sign in as eval (username eval, password momentic-eval-1).
Click the avatar in the top-right corner and choose "Sign Out". You land on the public home page, signed out (the header offers "Sign In").

The full Repository settings page appears again with its forms filled in (Repository Name "harbor-handbook", Description "Engineering handbook and release planning for the Harbor team.", the Danger Zone buttons below) and with the signed-in header chrome (notification bell, avatar menu).
Press Reload: only then does the site redirect to the Sign In page.
bugs.reason: The page comes from the browser's own history cache with no server request, and a reload goes to Sign In, so no session survives. Gitea chooses this on purpose: the source comments that 'max-age=0 + must-revalidate' is preferred instead of 'no-store' because browsers may restore input fields after navigate-back.

bugs.name: Creating a branch protection rule reports 'Branch protection for rule ... has been updated'
bugs.summary: The page shows "Branch protection for rule \"agent5-branch\" has been updated." although I had just created the rule and never edited an existing one. (on /eval/agent5-vis-probe/settings/branches)
bugs.expected: After creating a new protection rule the message tells the person the rule was created (e.g. "has been added"), not that an existing rule was updated.
bugs.actual: The page shows "Branch protection for rule \"agent5-branch\" has been updated." although I had just created the rule and never edited an existing one.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open https://5503-imv8yr62nz49o7qx2vsk0.e2b.app/eval/agent5-vis-probe/settings/branches (repo I created, agent5-vis-probe).
Click "Add New Rule" (the page had "There are no protected branches.").
Type agent5-branch into "Protected Branch Name Pattern" and click "Save Rule".
bugs.reason: Wording preference: the Save Rule form is a single create-or-update handler with one success string, and 'branch protection for rule X has been updated' still tells the user correctly that the protection was saved. The rule is created as requested and nothing is misreported about the data.

bugs.name: Push-mirror address without a scheme answers 'You are not allowed to import local repositories.'
bugs.summary: The page reloads with an error banner reading \"You are not allowed to import local repositories.\" — no word that the address is malformed — even though the server setting and permissions were never involved; the same address type given a scheme is answered correctly with \"The provided URL is invalid. Only http(s):// or git:// locations can be used for mirroring.\" (on /eval/agent8-mirror-probe/settings)
bugs.expected: The message says that the address is not a valid repository URL (or the same \"The provided URL is invalid...\" message), so the person knows to fix the address rather than thinking a permission blocks them.
bugs.actual: The page reloads with an error banner reading \"You are not allowed to import local repositories.\" — no word that the address is malformed — even though the server setting and permissions were never involved; the same address type given a scheme is answered correctly with \"The provided URL is invalid. Only http(s):// or git:// locations can be used for mirroring.\"
reproSteps: Sign in as eval / momentic-eval-1 and open https://5503-imv8yr62nz49o7qx2vsk0.e2b.app/eval/agent8-mirror-probe/settings (Mirror Settings block).
Type "not a url" into "Git Remote Repository URL" and click "Add Push Mirror".
bugs.reason: Deliberate: a remote address with no scheme is treated as a local filesystem path ('Remote address can be HTTP/HTTPS/Git URL or local path'), and local paths are refused for users who may not import local repositories, with exactly this message. 'not a url' is therefore handled as a local path, not as a malformed URL.
